stories.headline: What we learned: Selfless Lions maul Crows to leave Hawks shaking in their boots
stories.summary: From 53-point losers to 53-point winners, nobody rebounds like Brisbane. The three-peat is firmly on track.
stories.body:
GABBA -- Brisbane thrashed Adelaide on Saturday evening to book a fifth consecutive AFL preliminary final berth and send a major warning to the league's remaining finalists that its three-peat is firmly on track.

The Lions rebounded in style from last week's humbling defeat in Sydney and will now face Hawthorn at the MCG for a place in yet another Grand Final.

Here are three things we learned from the game:

The Lions are just two wins away from a magical dynasty ... and who would bet against them?
No team knows how to shake off a difficult loss quite like Brisbane. The Lions couldn't have played worse if they tried in last week's 53-point qualifying final defeat to Sydney at the SCG. The Swans, fresh off one of the most difficult fortnights in club history, caught lightning in a bottle and had the reigning champs rattled in the opening minutes. All of Brisbane's prime movers were well below their best and at no stage did they look like working their way into the contest. But that was last week.

Seven days later the Lions side showed why they are the back-to-back reigning premiers, bouncing back in emphatic style to record a 53-point win of their own, a crushing defeat of Adelaide to once again book a place in the last four. Brisbane flew out the gate, enjoyed the first 10 inside 50s of the night and put five goals on the Crows in just seven minutes and 13 seconds. By quarter-time it was 42-15 -- the Lions' highest score in the first quarter of a final since 1999.

So many of Brisbane's stars bounced back from their poor outings the week before. Charlie Cameron was electric with five goals. Zac Bailey, fresh from an eight-year contract extension during the week, kicked three goals from his 23 disposals. Kai Lohmann and Cam Rayner provided headaches in the front half all night. Will Ashcroft returned to finals Will Ashcroft (more on him later).

The ability to immediately respond has been an enviable trait of Brisbane over the past 12 months. Last year, the Lions were also humbled in a road qualifying final. They then won their next three finals to lift the premiership cup. In fact, since 2022 this club is now 11-2 in win-or-go-home finals.

Even this year the Lions have been quick to make amends for their most inexplicable losses. A 44-point defeat to the Swans in Round 1 was followed by a 33-point win against the Saints. The 76-point loss to the Blues late in the season was followed by a 67-point crushing of the Hawks. Even the rough three-game stretch midyear that had the footy world questioning their hunger was followed by wins in 10 of their final 11 home-and-away games.

The Lions will now travel to the MCG to battle Hawthorn for a place in a fourth consecutive Grand Final. Just two wins separate this resilient club from a stunning three-peat, are you brave enough to tip against them?

Despite the reports and the blowout, Matthew Nicks should remain safe in his role
Adelaide's finals road came to an abrupt end on Saturday evening in Brisbane. It's a loss that will no doubt sting for some time, but there's certainly no shame in falling to the back-to-back reigning champs on their home deck, right?

The Lions were clearly the better side on the night but the difference really was the burst in the opening minutes and another similarly scary attacking onslaught midway through the second term.

Perhaps Adelaide threw its biggest punch last week against the Bulldogs after rumours began circulating that coach Matthew Nicks could be out of a job should his side fail to win the home elimination final. That seemed wildly unfair at the time and even more ridiculous now they've taken it up to Brisbane.

There should be absolutely zero pressure on Nicks. At the end of the day, a coach's job is to win games. Since the beginning of last year, Nicks has orchestrated 34 wins. Only Brisbane's Chris Fagan, Geelong's Chris Scott, and Fremantle's Justin Longmuir boast more in that time. The Crows have also only suffered two heavy defeats in that period (one of them was tonight). For reference, Brisbane's had seven. Anyone who has built that type of enviable record over a two-year period deserves, at the very least, the respect of not being made to feel as if they're on the coaching hotseat.

Why is there this unfair expectation that Nicks and the Crows should be achieving so much more than they are? Even the most one-eyed Adelaide supporter would concede this side's probably not a top three team on paper, so finishing the season in fifth or sixth place should hardly be considered a failed campaign. Until the Crows are heading backwards, Nicks should not have to worry about his job security.

Will Ashcroft really should have been an All-Australian over Murphy Reid
Two-time Norm Smith Medal winner Will Ashcroft etched the latest chapter into his remarkable finals legacy on Saturday evening, turning in a dominant display against the Crows to propel Brisbane into yet another preliminary final.

It continues a dominant season for the young Lion who is not only the bookmakers' favourite to be best on ground on Grand Final day for a third time in succession, but is widely tipped to finish in the top five of this year's Brownlow Medal count. And yet, amazingly, Ashcroft wasn't selected in last month's All-Australian team.

Second year Docker Murphy Reid was someone who did receive a blazer. So, let's compare the pair:

You be the judge of who deserved to be included in the prestigious team.

Both Reid and Ashcroft were unusually quiet in their side's qualifying final losses last week. Both lifted on semifinal weekend, but Ashcroft's 30 disposals, 13 score involvements, six clearances, seven inside 50s, seven marks, and almost 500 metres gained against the Crows were just about best on ground numbers. And while finals performances don't count towards the All-Australian team, Ashcroft's latest outing only highlights how much of a blunder it was not having him in the 2026 team.

stories.headline: Arsenal's Gabriel 'eager' to take another Champions League final penalty: 'If it happens again, I'll be there'
stories.summary: Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhães has said that he is "eager" for another chance to take a penalty in a Champions League final.
stories.body:
Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhães has said told ESPN that he is "eager" for another chance to take a penalty in a Champions League final after the heartbreak of missing the crucial spot kick in last season's final against Paris Saint-Germain.

Following an earlier miss from Eberechi Eze in the shootout, Arsenal's hopes of winning their first European trophy rested on the shoulders of the Brazil defender who ultimately sent the ball over the crossbar to crown PSG champions for a second consecutive season.

Gabriel, a stalwart character of the Arsenal defence, told ESPN Brasil that if he was in a similar position again, he would take another penalty.

"I couldn't let a single missed penalty erase everything I'd achieved during the season," he said.

"So, I just thank God for the opportunity to have been there in that moment, it's part of the football.

"But I'm definitely eager for another chance, if it happens again, I'll be there, and if I have to take the penalty, I'll take it. So, that's it."

Arsenal were praised throughout last season's campaign for their solid defence, conceding just seven goals throughout their European campaign.

Gabriel thanked the fans for their continued support despite their European season ending on a sour note.

"I only have to thank the fans," he told ESPN Brasil. "Ever since the final, I've just received a lot of support from them, you know. They were incredible to me, sending very positive messages.

"But like I said, it's part of football. I'm here, and it's not the first time something like this has happened. So, as I said, if there's another penalty for me to take, I'll take it."

Mikel Arteta's side are yet to drop points this season but face a stiff test when they take on Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

stories.headline: Spanish Grand Prix: Lewis Hamilton crashes in Madrid before ignoring Ferrari instruction to stop car
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli set the pace in the final practice session of the Spanish Grand Prix in what was a heavily-disrupted session.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton crashed out of final practice for the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.

The seven-time world champion lost control of his Ferrari under braking for the final corner and hit the barriers.

Hamilton was able to reverse out of the tyre wall and attempted to complete a full lap back to the pits, ignoring multiple instructions from his team to park his broken car.

"Stop the car," Hamilton's race engineer Carlo Santi said.

"Car is going," Hamilton replied, with his damaged front wing lodged under the front-right of his machine.

Santi was back on the radio again. "Stop in the safest place possible," he said.

Hamilton replied: "If I can make it back I will and if I can't I will stop safely."

Sanit said: "We have a puncture on the front. Stop the car."

"I can see that," Hamilton said in response as he continued against his team's wishes in attempting to get back to his garage.

After completing two thirds of the lap, Hamilton eventually pulled over to the side of the track. Hamilton emerged from his car which was taken back to the pits on a flat-bed truck.

Hamilton was on course to set the quickest lap of the session so far prior to his accident.

- Spanish Grand Prix: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli sets pace in second practice, George Russell fifth

- Spanish Grand Prix: Everything you need to know about F1's brand-new Madring

- 'The most risky on the calendar': F1 drivers react to 'crazy' Madring layout ahead of Spanish Grand Prix

After a lengthy delay, the running restarted before Ollie Bearman also fell victim to the Madring.

The British driver spun out at Turn 10 and slammed into the barrier sustaining heavy damage to the left-hand side of his Haas.

Bearman was uninjured in the high-speed crash but his mechanics will face a race against time to repair his car for qualifying which gets under way at 4 p.m. local time (3 p.m. BST/10am ET).

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli set the fastest time, 0.166 seconds clear of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, with Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris third and fourth respectively for McLaren.

Max Verstappen finished fifth, a place clear of George Russell, who was seven tenths slower than Mercedes teammate Antonelli.

stories.headline: Suns' Mark Williams to miss months after shoulder surgery
stories.summary: Phoenix Suns center Mark Williams had surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss several months.
stories.body:
Phoenix Suns center Mark Williams had surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss several months, the team announced Friday.

The 7-foot-1 Williams, 24, who signed a fully guaranteed three-year, $38 million deal to return to the Suns in free agency, suffered the injury during a recent offseason workout.

He was coming off the healthiest season of his four-year NBA career, appearing in 60 games after a previous high of 44. He averaged 11.7 points, 8.0 rebounds and 0.9 blocks in 23.6 minutes per game.

Williams arrived in Phoenix in a 2025 draft night deal from Charlotte, after the Hornets' first attempt to trade him was rescinded shortly at that year's trade deadline. Williams took over as the Suns' starting center and was part of a group that helped Phoenix beat preseason expectations in earning a playoff berth.

He has career averages of 12 points, 8.5 rebounds and one block per game.

Without Williams, the Suns will likely lean on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach to play the bulk of the minutes at center this season.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Team USA hears coach's message entering FIBA World Cup semis
stories.summary: As Team USA gears up for the FIBA World Cup semifinals, it feels it is poised to play its best basketball because of how coach Kara Lawson has challenged its players.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- As Team USA gears up for the FIBA World Cup semifinals, it feels it is poised to play its best basketball at the right time -- in part because of how coach Kara Lawson has challenged her players.

After a 55-52 victory against Italy on Sunday in which the U.S. trailed in the fourth quarter, Lawson implored her team in a postgame locker room address -- a clip of which was posted on social media -- to "let this be the last time that a team plays with more passion than us throughout the course of the game. Let this be the last time that all 12 don't show up to compete at a high level."

Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier said the team heard Lawson's message.

"I think the team received it really well because we felt it too," Collier said. "We know that we didn't give our best. We didn't obviously play our best. We could have done a lot better. And she's absolutely right. We're playing for our country right now, and it's inexcusable the way that we came out in that game, and so I think the team took it as a challenge, like she's right.

"... I don't think we're going to have that problem again."

The team's response has been evident. Wins by 41 and 52 points over Czechia and Hungary, respectively, have secured Team USA's spot in the semifinals for the 11th consecutive World Cup.

USA Basketball has been one of the most dominant sports dynasties over the past three decades, dropping just one game at the Olympics or World Cup since 1994.

Italy, however, came close to handing Team USA its first loss in a major international tournament since the 2006 World Cup semifinals, holding the U.S. to its lowest-scoring output in a World Cup game since 1971.

The game was a "wake-up call, probably that everybody needed because ... it is hard to play in these tournaments," two-time MVP Breanna Stewart told ESPN. "It is hard to be USA. It is hard to always have to have this incredible excellence, but that's the standard that we have."

Lawson said her postgame message stemmed from wanting to be direct and transparent, especially in such a short tournament -- with six games in 10 days -- where time is of the essence.

She credited her team's ability to make winning plays down the stretch, particularly its stout defense, but was more focused on ensuring her group doesn't fall short in bringing the necessary intangibles to win games.

"Let this be the last time that we lack a resilient mindset because we're so upset that we're not scoring the way we're normally scoring," Lawson told her team after the Italy game. "Your contribution has to be your passion, your energy, your intensity that you play with."

Sue Bird, the managing director for the women's national team, told ESPN that Lawson was "spot on" and that what happened in the Italy game "was great" because the team found a way to win despite having a "terrible game."

"You want to put the team on alert," Bird said. "Like, that's not acceptable because of, not the ball going in or not, not a turnover, but how we played. So I thought she did a great job, but having the balance of like, but we just f---ing figured out a way to win in a really hard game."

Added Collier: "It showed us that we have that fight in us. ... Hopefully we won't have to use it in that close of a situation, but at least we know that we have it, and we can dig into it if needed."

Amid the break in WNBA play, Team USA has been together in Berlin for less than two weeks, and with A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum being late scratches, the roster ended up with seven players making their first appearance at a major international tournament for the senior national team -- all while the parity among international teams has never been closer.

"You're going to get everybody's best shot," Las Vegas Aces star Chelsea Gray said. "It's a different level of physicality. It's a different kind of mindset that you have to have in the way you play over here with FIBA, and you can't take possessions off offensively and defensively. And you were able to see that in the way we competed the last two games."

USA bounced back by playing its best two-way basketball of the tournament against Hungary, but the path forward won't get any easier. Spain should be its toughest test yet, and either France -- the 2024 Olympic silver medalists -- or Germany -- the hometown darlings -- would await in the gold medal game.

"These four teams are great," Lawson said. "Each of these four teams is talented enough to win the whole thing."

Lawson credited Spain, which has a slew of WNBA players, including Megan DiLeo, Awa Fam and Maria Conde, for its frontcourt depth and skilled guards.

"I can't say enough about their quality, quality at every position," Lawson said, "and so we're going to have to play really well."

The U.S. beat Spain 84-70 at the qualifying tournament in March in Puerto Rico.

"I feel like they're playing at an even higher level, and they, just like us, have gotten better as every game has gone on in this tournament," Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark said. "So I'm just excited. These are the games you get really, really amped up about and you see what you're made of."

stories.headline: Dylan Larkin to attend Red Wings camp despite trade request
stories.summary: Longtime captain Dylan Larkin will be at Red Wings training camp despite requesting a trade this offseason. Though Larkin will be in attendance, the team said it will begin the season without a captain.
stories.body:
Longtime Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin will report to training camp in Detroit next week despite his summer trade request.

However the Red Wings announced that they will begin the season without a captain.

"Over the past couple of weeks, Red Wings leadership and I have had several in-depth discussions. I've appreciated those candid conversations, and I will be at training camp with my teammates," Larkin said in a statement. "When new leadership is in place, we'll talk further about the direction of the team. We will keep those conversations private, and I will keep my focus on the season ahead and on the guys in that room."

In July, shortly after Larkin's trade request became public, the Red Wings announced that Steve Yzerman would no longer be the team's general manager. Yzerman, a franchise legend and Hall of Famer, had been GM since 2019. Detroit entered a rebuild in that time and hasn't made the playoffs in 10 years.

In a statement, the Red Wings said they "look forward to seeing Dylan and his teammates at Little Caesars for the start of training camp," which begins Sept. 17.

"Any further discussions or decisions regarding this topic will be made once new hockey operations leadership is in place," the team said.

The Red Wings have hired a search firm, which has been conducting interviews for a new general manager.

Larkin, 30, grew up in nearby Waterford, Michigan, and played at the University of Michigan. He was selected by his hometown team in the first round of the 2014 NHL draft.

He debuted in the 2015-16 season for the Red Wings, and the team made the playoffs in his rookie season -- the final year of the franchise's NHL-record 25-year playoff streak. Detroit lost to Tampa Bay in five games in the first round and hasn't returned since.

Larkin was a key member of the 2026 U.S. men's Olympic team that won its first gold medal since 1980. He was especially important defensively and on special teams, part of a penalty killing unit that went a flawless 18-for-18 in Milan.

The Minnesota Wild -- led by Bill Guerin, also the general manager of Team USA -- have tried to acquire Larkin, according to sources. However the sides have been at a stalemate this summer, especially as Detroit's GM seat is vacant.

Larkin had been Detroit's captain since 2021. He ranks 10th in franchise history in both goals (276) and points (643).

The Red Wings' offseason has been defined by uncertainty. That led in part to the free agent departure of Patrick Kane, who returned to the Chicago Blackhawks. Another key piece of business that's unresolved: ascending star defenseman Simon Edvinsson is due for a contract extension.

stories.headline: What We Learned: Sharks rediscover their bite; Trindall unlocks Hynes
stories.summary: Braydon Trindall allowed Nicho Hynes to play his best and the Sharks reaped the rewards, while the Cowboys season is over. Here's what we learned from the game.
stories.body:
Cronulla have kept their premiership hopes alive with a 26-16 elimination-final victory over North Queensland at Allianz Stadium.

The Sharks scored five tries in an encouraging attacking display, with Sione Katoa crossing twice before Nicho Hynes produced the defining moment to establish an unassailable lead.

Cronulla will now face the loser of Sunday's qualifying final between Penrith and the Sydney Roosters, while North Queensland's season is over.

Here are three things we learned from the game:

The Sharks thrive on confidence

Cronulla reminded us that confidence remains their greatest asset. When the tide turns in their direction, the fire is quickly lit -- and few teams can extinguish it.

Sione Katoa's intercept try was the perfect example.

The winger read Scott Drinkwater's pass, plucked the ball out of the air and raced 60 metres to restore Cronulla's lead. After Katoa crossed again shortly after halftime, the Sharks began playing with greater speed, freedom and ambition.

They nearly travelled the length of the field to score again immediately after Katoa's second, with the movement ultimately forcing a Cowboys error and earning Cronulla a scrum.

A similar surge followed Will Kennedy's try in the 60th minute. The Sharks again swept upfield before Hynes produced a piece of individual brilliance, dummying his way through the defensive line and crossing to push the margin out to 14 points.

It was the type of attacking football Cronulla are capable of when their confidence is flowing. Players support through the middle, passes stick and Hynes becomes increasingly willing to challenge the defensive line.

The concern for Craig Fitzgibbon's men is what happens when momentum is not behind them.

Whether their next opponent is Penrith or the Roosters, Cronulla are unlikely to be afforded the same opportunities to build confidence through repeat attacking movements. Both sides will attempt to slow the Sharks down and deny them the momentum that fuelled Saturday night's victory.

Cronulla showed how dangerous they can be once the fire is burning. The next challenge is learning how to light it themselves when a game is not naturally flowing their way.

Trindall's return unlocks Hynes

Nicho Hynes was back to his dangerous best on Saturday night, which should come as little surprise with Braydon Trindall restored alongside him.

Hynes acknowledged earlier in the week that Trindall performs much of Cronulla's traditional halfback work despite wearing the No. 6 jersey. That dynamic was evident against the Cowboys.

Trindall assumed greater control of Cronulla's shape and kicking game, allowing Hynes to pick his moments and play with freedom as a running threat.

The Dally M medallist ran the ball 15 times for more than 120 metres, broke five tackles and scored a sensational solo try. Receiving the ball close to the Cowboys' line, Hynes shaped to pass before stepping through the defence and accelerating into open space.

It was a decisive play from a player who has endured no shortage of scrutiny over his performances in big games.

Trindall's value to Cronulla extends beyond his own statistics. His presence gives the Sharks greater direction and reduces the burden on Hynes to organise every attacking set, kick long and then manufacture the decisive play.

Hynes is at his most dangerous when he can survey the defence and choose when to inject himself. With Trindall steering the side, Cronulla's highest-paid player can concentrate on becoming its most damaging one.

Drinkwater remains the ultimate high-risk, high-reward player

Scott Drinkwater was once again at his rocks-and-diamonds best, producing two try assists and four line-break assists while also committing four errors.

It can certainly be argued that the Cowboys would not have remained in the contest without him. Drinkwater directly created two of North Queensland's three tries and converted both, playing a role in 12 of their 16 points.

His sweeping cut-out pass to create the Cowboys' opening try was Drinkwater at his creative best: daring, instinctive and capable of seeing an opportunity that few other players would attempt.

But the same appetite for risk also produced costly moments.

His intercept pass gifted Katoa a 60-metre try at a crucial stage of the first half, while his handling and decision-making errors repeatedly halted North Queensland's momentum.

That contrast has always defined Drinkwater's game. He can manufacture points from nothing, but his determination to find the decisive play can occasionally hand momentum to the opposition.

It is his X factor that prompted St George Illawarra to sign him on a multiyear deal from 2027. The Dragons are betting that his creativity can transform their attack, while accepting the volatility that comes with it.

Saturday night provided the complete Drinkwater experience: breathtaking creativity, costly mistakes and a willingness to continue chasing the match regardless of what had happened on the previous play.

For North Queensland, however, the rewards were not quite enough to outweigh the risks.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye Bournemouth defender to replace Shaw
stories.summary: Manchester United see AFC Bournemouth defender Adrien Truffert as a future replacement for Luke Shaw. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United see AFC Bournemouth defender Adrien Truffert as a future replacement for Luke Shaw, while Liverpool remain keen on Internazionale midfielder Aleksandar Stankovic. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- AFC Bournemouth are demanding a £60 million fee for the transfer of defender Adrien Truffert, with Manchester United reportedly seeing the left back as a possible long-term successor for Luke Shaw. TEAMtalk says that United are keen on Truffert, but Bournemouth are insistent on their valuation and are also holding firm in their desire for £100 million fees to let midfielder Alex Scott, striker Junior Kroupi or forward Rayan leave. United have also been linked with Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, 20, but the German club aren't willing to consider anything less than a "very substantial offer" according to TuttoJuve.

- Liverpool remain keen on Internazionale midfielder Aleksandar Stankovic after enquiring about him while negotiating Curtis Jones' €35 million move to San Siro, according to TEAMtalk. The Reds used the talks as an opportunity to check on the 21-year-old's availability, with the Nerazzurri having exercised their €23 million option to re-sign him from Club Brugge earlier in the summer. Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur had also shown an interest in the Serbia international during the summer.

- Real Madrid striker Endrick is facing an uncertain future despite being ready to return from injury, says Sport. Endrick, 20, has struggled to assert himself in the Madrid first XI since his €72 million move from Palmeiras in 2024 and spent time on loan at Lyon last season. Now Carlos Espí has been signed as new boss Jose Mourinho's second-choice striker behind Kylian Mbappé, the future of Endrick is up for debate and he will need to prove himself in the coming months if he wants to stay.

- Ronald Araújo's future at Barcelona is increasingly dependent on the stance of manager Hansi Flick, according to TEAMtalk. The Liverpool loanee's summer move to Anfield came about following Flick's admission that he couldn't guarantee Araujo the game time he wanted at Barca. Liverpool have a permanent option to sign the 27-year-old for €55 million and have been delighted with his start to life in England, but are in no rush to decide his long-term future.

- Sources close to Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison have indicated that other clubs are interested after he rejected a move to Vasco da Gama, as reported by UOL, although no clubs were named in the report. Vasco's board has already been informed by the 29-year-old that he won't be joining them. The Brazilian club tried to sign him on a permanent deal, but he wanted it to be short-term and would have joined on loan if it was allowed.

Other rumors
- Arsenal and Atletico Madrid are monitoring Roma right back Wesley. (Ekrem Konur)

- Liverpool are not planning on holding talks about Virgil van Dijk's contract until next year. (Football Insider)

- Negotiations are underway for Internazionale to extend Federico Dimarco's contract until 2030. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Juventus are keeping an eye on Sassuolo midfielder Darryl Bakola with January or next summer in mind. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Crystal Palace and Fulham are both interested in Brest center back Raphael Le Guen. (Le10 Sport)

stories.headline: NFL Week 1 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines
stories.summary: Could DeVonta Smith find the end zone in Week 1? Will the Jets finally intercept a pass? What will Aidan Hutchinson's stat line look like Sunday?
stories.byline: Matt Bowen, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody, Ben Solak and Seth Walder
stories.body:
The 2026 NFL season is underway, with the Seahawks and 49ers already crowned as winners in Week 1. But what will happen in the remaining 14 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright, Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projected out stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen suggests three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Broncos upset the Chiefs? Will Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson score a touchdown? And is Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis flying under the fantasy radar? Let's make 15 big predictions for all the action on Sunday and Monday.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Wild-card predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

New York Jets +1.5 at Tennessee Titans

New York's clearest strength can take advantage of Tennessee's biggest weakness Sunday. The Jets added more playmakers to their pass rush alongside Will McDonald IV, including No. 2 pick David Bailey, while the Titans' offensive line came in at 26th in Mike Clay's positional group rankings. That pressure could force Titans QB Cam Ward into fumble risk and the hero-ball mistakes that hurt him last season.

Denver Broncos +2.5 at Kansas City Chiefs

Denver has the strong defense to neutralize a Chiefs offense with real questions. Kansas City has vulnerabilities on the offensive line, quarterback Patrick Mahomes is returning from major knee surgery, and the Chiefs' passing game was already declining before his injury in Week 15. Denver's biggest edge on Monday night should be making Mahomes uncomfortable and turning this into another tight game between the AFC West foes.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Aidan Hutchinson, Edge, Detroit Lions: 2.0 sacks, 7 pressures, 25% pass rush win rate

I'm already extremely bullish on Hutchinson, who led my seasonlong sack projections. And he's set up extremely well for a lightning-quick start.

The Lions are seven-point favorites over the Saints, which means there's a high likelihood New Orleans will be behind and forced into must-pass situations. Quarterback Tyler Shough took sacks at a high 8.3% rate last season, and Hutchinson should have favorable matchups against left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. or right tackle Taliese Fuaga. Both tackles were well below average in pass block win rate last season.

Adonai Mitchell, WR, New York Jets: 5 receptions, 84 receiving yards, 1 touchdown

I have been hyping up Mitchell for a while and strongly believe this is the season when it all comes together. The case for Mitchell is simple: He gets open.

Over the past two seasons combined, Mitchell ranks seventh among wide receivers in ESPN's open score. The Titans' two new cornerbacks, Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott, were both below average last season in my pre-throw cornerback positioning metric.

Jordyn Brooks, LB, Miami Dolphins: 14 tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 45% run stop win rate

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak used a run-heavy offense last season in Seattle. I have to imagine he'll want to do the same with Kirk Cousins, 38, at quarterback and a lacking receiver group that lost Brock Bowers (meniscus trim) for Week 1. Add in that the Raiders are favored -- therefore more likely to be leading -- and that should equate to even more rushes for rookie Mike Washington Jr. and (presumably) Ashton Jeanty (ankle).

Brooks is the defender most likely to absorb those runs and convert them into tackles. Last season, he ranked fifth among linebackers in tackle rate versus run plays (25%) and 12th in run stop win rate (37%).

Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers

Jalen Coker, WR, Carolina Panthers (rostered in 51.4% of ESPN leagues)

From Week 8 through Carolina's wild-card loss, Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. He flashed his upside in the playoffs against the Rams, finishing with nine receptions for 134 yards and a touchdown.

Coker is projected for the second-most targets on the Panthers behind Tetairoa McMillan, and both receivers have a favorable matchup against the Bears in Week 1. Chicago's defense allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers last season.

Malik Willis, QB, Miami Dolphins (22.1%)

Since 2016, there have been 23 seasons in which a quarterback started at least 16 games and averaged at least five rushing attempts per game. Those quarterbacks combined to average 21.2 fantasy points per game. Willis should easily surpass that number of attempts in Week 1, which keeps him fantasy relevant despite having one of the league's weaker supporting casts. Plus, the Raiders allowed 16.0 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks last season.

Michael Mayer, TE, Las Vegas Raiders (7.0%)

Brock Bowers will miss Week 1 after undergoing a meniscus trim, which should lead to more targets for Mayer and wide receiver Tre Tucker (29.3%). In four games without Bowers last season, Mayer averaged 6.0 targets and 10.9 fantasy points per game.

Quarterback Kirk Cousins has also leaned on tight ends throughout his career, and Miami allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to the position last season.

Bowen predicts three players to score touchdowns

Jake Ferguson, TE, Dallas Cowboys

Ferguson is a priority red zone target for quarterback Dak Prescott in this offense. He saw 23 red zone targets last season, with seven of his eight touchdown grabs coming on throws inside the 20-yard line. Against the Giants on Sunday night, he can get loose on play-action concepts in the red zone. Look for him to the get the ball on corner routes and seams.

D'Andre Swift, RB, Chicago Bears

In coach Ben Johnson's zone run game, Swift should see touches in scoring position. Last season, he had nine rushing touchdowns and 10 carries inside the 5-yard line. He'll get opportunities against a Panthers' defense that allowed 19 rushing scores in 2025 (third most in the NFL). Plus, Swift can create explosive plays as a receiver in the screen game. Those can lead to the end zone, too.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

After A.J. Brown was traded to the Patriots, Smith elevated to the No. 1 role in Philly. So, the volume will be there for him versus the Commanders' defense. Plus, we should expect more West Coast passing concepts under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Watch for Smith, who has 12 touchdown receptions over his past two seasons, to score on a catch-and-run target.

Solak makes four other wild-card predictions

The Jets will snag a pick

For those who (understandably) wiped the 2025 Jets season from their memory: They were the first team in NFL history to fail to secure an interception over a full season. There's no level of overall team badness that explains that -- it takes truly terrible luck.

But fear no more! The Aaron Glenn Jets should finally get their interception in Week 1 against Cam Ward. Tennessee's offense is new across the board, with changes to its offensive coordinator and two primary receivers. And the Jets should have enough of a pass rush to force some errant throws.

The Dolphins will win

Before you tell me there's no shot, remember how confident we all were in the Rams' dominance ... and how did they look Thursday night? Now, the Dolphins' game against the Raiders is not in Australia, but Week 1 is known for weird results.

With Willis as one of the league's preeminent dual-threat quarterbacks (he really is as good of a runner as Jayden Daniels), new Dolphins offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik can deploy a ton of surprising wrinkles of which the Raiders' defensive staff has no film. The absence of Bowers is also huge because the Raiders aren't loaded with impressive pass catchers behind him. Imagine if we start the season with the Dolphins having a better record than the Rams!

A kickoff will be returned for a touchdown

The kickoff rules changed last season, and it had a great effect with more enjoyable returns. Now that special teams coordinators have spent an entire offseason studying the dynamic kickoff and what coverage weaknesses it might have, I think we'll see more designed returns (reverses, blocking schemes, etc.) in an effort to steal some points.

A team will attempt a Hail Mary, it will fall incomplete, and the game will be ruled over. But then upon review, one second will be put back on the clock, a second Hail Mary will be attempted, this one will be completed, and the winner of the game will switch.

Sounds improbable, I know. But I've seen it happen!

stories.headline: What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is facing 100 drivers in a unique event called Max vs. 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 challengers, starting from the back of the grid.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is taking part in a unique event called Max vs 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 drivers, starting from the back of the grid.

The 28-year-old currently races in F1, the highest tier in motorsport. He is one of the fiercest competitors out there and is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking.

But if you have never heard of him, or want to learn more, here is everything you need to know.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

Who is Max Verstappen?
Verstappen was born in Belgium to his Dutch father Jos and his Belgian mother Sophie. His father raced in F1 between 1994-2003 and had two podium finishes, while his mother competed in karts. He currently resides in Monaco.

Who does he race for?
Verstappen started racing go-karts when he was just four years old and started to compete in championships at seven.

He then made his way through the ranks winning several world and European titles in 2013. He raced just one season in Formula 3 before skipping Formula 2 and heading straight to Formula 1.

In 2015, he signed for Red Bull junior team Toro Rosso at the age of 17 before he was promoted to Red Bull a year later.

He then went on to become the youngest ever grand prix winner after taking victory at the Spanish Grand Prix and has been at Red Bull ever since, becoming the most successful driver at the team.

He signed a long-term contract back in March 2022 to stay at the Milton Keynes-based team until the end of 2028, and before the Dutch Grand Prix this year he penned a new deal keeping him at the team until 2030.

What has he achieved?
It was clear from the early days that Verstappen was going to be an exceptional racing driver and he's become a phenomenon since with a killer instinct.

He's had 244 race starts in F1 and has been on the top step of the podium 71 times. He's been on the podium 131 times and is just two pole positions away from reaching 50 career poles.

The Dutchman has four world championships which he won back-to-back in a dominant Red Bull era between 2021-2024.

He also has an impressive list of achievements to his name, one being in 2023 where he recorded the most wins [19] and the most podium finishes [21] in a single season. He also recorded 10 consecutive race victories.

When is Max vs 100?
The event is taking place on Sept. 16 and will be streamed live on Disney+.

Why is he racing in Max vs 100?

Verstappen has never been shy of getting his teeth stuck into other forms of motorsport away from Formula 1. He most recently made his debut at the iconic Nürburgring 24 Hours in May, driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3.

This will be a slightly different challenge for the Dutchman, but no doubt one he will enjoy with his competitive nature.

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," Verstappen said. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return."

The event is taking place at Silverstone in the U.K. and a circuit has been purpose-built for the occasion. It's set to be the biggest go-kart event in the world.

- Max Verstappen deal: Good news for Red Bull and F1, bad news for the driver market

- Max Verstappen ends F1 speculation by signing new Red Bull contract to 2030

How is his 2026 F1 season going?
The 2026 season is one with big regulation and rules changes and Red Bull are currently at the back of the front running teams, but are ahead of the midfield pack.

Verstappen is still searching for his first race win of the season, but has been on the podium four times.

He's currently sixth in the title championship and is 130 points adrift from title leader Kimi Antonelli.

stories.headline: 'The Hoop Collective': Episodes of Brian Windhorst's NBA podcast

stories.body:
"The Hoop Collective" podcast, hosted by ESPN's Brian Windhorst, releases episodes every Monday, Wednesday and Friday during the NBA season and Tuesday and Friday during the offseason. Windhorst and his guests break down what's happening on and off the court, evaluating the trends you need to know and examining the latest news from across the NBA.

'The Hoop Collective' episodes

Sept. 11: Why the future of NBA Europe is uncertain

Brian is joined by Aris Barkas, the publishing director of Eurohoops, to discuss the future plans for the NBA in Europe, including if it's actually feasible, how it could possibly work out and the current state of European basketball.

Sept. 8: What history may tell us about Clippers' future + key signings in the West
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to cover the latest fallout from the LA Clippers' punishment after the NBA announced its punishments for the franchise's off-the-court dealings with Kawhi Leonard. They discuss what league history could tell us about what's ahead for the Clippers and how LA got into this situation. They then close on key deals in the West, including Ben Simmons signing with the Sacramento Kings and Amen Thompson's extension with the Houston Rockets.

Windhorst on the league's reaction to the Clippers' punishment: "I think Steve Balmer had support of his peers in this, even though these was pretty severe accusations.

"I'm not saying everybody again, but I think people wanted to believe him, his peers. I'm not talking about the other GMs. I'm not talking about the agents. ...

"So the word that was said to me by a very influential person was that the other owners, some of the other owners were aghast when they read this report. That was the word that was used to me, aghast. And regardless of what Steve says, the support that he had is no longer there."

Windhorst on the Clippers' best course of action now: "When the Wolves were found guilty, Glen Taylor said words that were not, "I'm guilty." Kevin McHale, who was the vice president of basketball operations, said, 'I didn't even know this existed.' You know, he pled ignorance.

"[Then] They thought about it. They ended up negotiating with the league office and they pled guilty. And two days after basically they raised the white flag in December, David Stern gave him back a pick and a year later he gave him back the second pick. Now he gave them back -- he took away five years of picks [previously] -- he gave them back Year 3 at first and then Year 5. It wasn't like he gave him back immediately. But I think the Clippers should study that."

MacMahon on why Houston extended Thompson now: "I've been telling you for a while just how much the Rockets value Thompson. If there's one untradeable player on the roster, it is him.

"According to their metrics, they think he's one of the top 10 -- and I might be inflating that number -- most valuable players in the league. Now, we can argue and we can debate and you can say that's ridiculous. I'm just telling you the way that they view him. And so for them to get a player they value that much on this deal is great value for them.

"And for Amen Thompson, $208 million fully guaranteed and there's no options either way in the deal, he's set for life. He wants to be in Houston. He's going to be in Houston."

Sept. 3: EMERGENCY POD: NBA announces Clippers' punishments after Kawhi probe
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to react to the hefty punishments handed down to the LA Clippers by the NBA after the investigation into Kawhi Leonard's off-court dealings. They break down what this means for the future of the Clippers, if the punishment makes sense and if this will impact Leonard's pending trade to the Toronto Raptors.

Topics:

7:04 :The Clippers' argument against the NBA in this

16:47: What comes next for the Clippers?

30:21: How will this punishment impact Kawhi?

32:56: Who was most impacted by this punishment?

43:56: Final thoughts on this punishment decision

MacMahon on why the penalty was so large for the Clippers: "The simple fact of the matter is this ain't the first time Steve Balmer's pulled this shady stuff. That did not help his case.

"They gave him a little slap on the wrist for the DeAndre Jordan stuff in 2015. $250,000 fine. It was 'Oh, whoops. We didn't know.' And then, there's the investigation for the Kawhi signing because, guess what? It's not like Uncle Dennis only asked the Clippers for a whole bunch of under-the-table stuff. He was asking everybody for under-the-table stuff. 'Oh, geez. You know, we were asked, but we didn't, you know, didn't give him anything' and and now this. So, in a way they're three-time losers."

Windhorst on the Clippers' best course of action following the ruling: "If they could get an agreement, if they could plead guilty, get an agreement and and say, 'We're not going to challenge any of these penalties.' And they get an agreement that there'll be no further penalties -- basically, they'll say that these five first-round picks are all-encompassing, they cover everything. It's a blanket agreement and [then] they keep their nose clean, and they do the Kawhi trade, they might be able to come out of this without four broken limbs. They may be able to come out of this with less damage."

MacMahon on one of the winners of the investigation: "I do think Adam Silver in a way is a winner of this because straight up, he had been soft on crime as the commissioner since, ironically, he booted the previous Clippers owner, which was completely different circumstances."

Sept. 1: How Steph Curry can decide Warriors' future and major questions for Pistons
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Anthony Slater to discuss Stephen Curry's future with the Golden State Warriors, including how a potential extension could determine the franchise's outlook. They then move on to the Jalen Duren-Detroit Pistons situation, as his restricted free agency continues. Will this cause major issues for the Pistons' season? Slater on the potential Curry extension in Golden State and why he could wait: "One of the things in discussions I've been having with people is this idea of, let's say he's like, '[Taking less money for the team is] something I'd think about.' I would be surprised if he locked into a number now because, as you just saw with Draymond Green, the Warriors and their legendary figures are willing to trust each other in business.

"Draymond Green willingly gave up $27 million and went into unrestricted free agency where he couldn't have got $27 million back, [but] under the understanding if business didn't work out, he would get that money back. If you're Steph, you say, 'OK, you know what? I'll give y'all a crack at going and trying to find some stuff, but if you don't, at the end of the day, if I come back and say, give me the full max, I get the full max.'

"So, to answer your question, he doesn't have to necessarily lock into it now because they can't really execute [upgrading the roster]. Even if they could say, 'Hey, here's a theory of what we could do. Here's another theory of what we could do,' he could just say, 'All right, well, I'll hold off for now and see if you can do it, but at the end of the day, if I want the max, give me the max.'"

MacMahon on the Duren-Detroit situation: "He just averaged 19 [points] and 11 [rebounds]. He's a big physical force with some skill. Unfortunately, and this is part of the complications here, is he also just had a really disappointing playoff performance. I would say in terms of individual playoff performances coming off of that All-NBA season, Jalen Duren might have been the most disappointing in the league.

I've talked to just executives from other teams around the league just kind of taking people's temperature and a lot of what I got is like, 'I can definitely see both sides of this,' because for the Pistons this is not an anti-Jalen Duren thing. This is a, 'We want to keep this core together.' By the way, they're also in the process of attempting to negotiate an extension with Ausar Thompson."

MacMahon on the Wembanyama-Jokic rivalry: "As much as Denver's summer was frankly a disaster, you can't just dismiss the Nuggets.

"Let me say this, Victor Wembanyama might be the most dominant defensive player in the history of the game. One guy he does not bother much is Nikola Jokic. Do you know what Joker's stats against Wemby are in seven games in the NBA? 37.3 points per game, 10.9 rebounds, 9.1 assists."

Obviously, I'm sure there were other Wolves that were involved as well, but obviously Ant, from what I understand, Ant was very excited. Ant, from what I am told, is very pleased by the Wolves' offseason. Going to get LaMelo [Ball], making this deal happen for Kuminga.

"I don't think Ant's a guy who stews and is angry, [but] the last time we saw Ant he was congratulating the other team with five minutes on the clock or whatever it was. I don't think he was thrilled with that situation."

MacMahon on what Minnesota needs from Kuminga: "I think a lot of this comes down to Kuminga's willingness to adapt his game to try to be a complementary player to try to fit in. There's going to be spacing concerns.

"He's not a great shooter. Jaden McDaniels' 3-point shot has kind of been up and down over the years. I think that's going to be critical. Now, Ant's a hell of a shooter. LaMelo Ball,you're going to guard him and you're going to guard him out to 30-plus feet because he'll launch it. And the percentages aren't awesome, but he's a threat, for sure. But with [Rudy] Gobert and Kuminga, you know Finch is going to have to figure out some spacing issues, but Kuminga's got to be a finisher. He's got to get off this idea that he's a ball-in-hand creator."

stories.headline: Fever's Sophie Cunningham not worried about off-court distractions
stories.summary: Sophie Cunningham says she is focusing on the Fever's remaining games and not the commotion around Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declaring for the WNBA draft.
stories.body:
Sophie Cunningham says she is focusing on the Indiana Fever's four remaining regular-season games and not the commotion around Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declaring themselves eligible for the WNBA draft.

"I'm gonna let them do them," Cunningham told ESPN on Friday as part of a wide-ranging interview. "I'm just focused on the Fever and on our sport. I think we have four more games left. I'm trying to just really dial in and keep the main thing the main thing."

Kanter Freedom, who posted his intention to play in the WNBA on social media Aug. 7, was ejected from the Fever's game against the Sky on Aug. 23 in Chicago following a verbal altercation with guard Natasha Cloud. He has since filed a lawsuit arguing his First Amendment rights had been violated.

White attended a Fever game against the Connecticut Sun on Aug. 28.

Cunningham said she supported restricting transgender girls and women from girls' and women's sports in an ESPN article published July 21.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that,'" Cunningham said in the article. "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

Rallies for and against transgender inclusion popped up at Fever games in the weeks after the article. The WNBA has been on a break since Aug. 31 while many of its stars, including the Fever's Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston, compete at the FIBA World Cup in Berlin.

The Fever, who return to the court next Friday in Toronto, are 26-14 and in fifth place in the standings. The team is battling for home-court advantage in the first round of the playoffs, which begin Sept. 27.

On Thursday, Cunningham, who is averaging 8.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game, relaunched her podcast with new host Drew Hanlen and a new name, "No Hesitation."

"I think this team has great potential to make a really great playoff run," Cunningham said. "And if I'm filling my brain and my energy with all that stuff, then it's taking away from the team. And so I'm just trying to stay here and let them do what they want to do."

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 35
Goals: 31
Assists: 14

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Sharks sink Cowboys to stay alive in NRL finals
stories.summary: Braydon Trindall has produced 80 of the gutsiest minutes in a Cronulla jersey, defying shoulder pain to boot the Sharks to a 26-16 knockout win over North Queensland.
stories.body:
Braydon Trindall has produced 80 of the gutsiest minutes in a Cronulla jersey, defying shoulder pain to boot the Sharks to a 26-16 knockout win over North Queensland.

After entering the finals with four losses from their past five games, Trindall's return helped the Sharks hit back in Saturday's elimination final at Allianz Stadium.

Sione Katoa scored a double to help end the season of the Cowboys side he will join next year, while Siosifa Talakai busted seven tackles and also scored Cronulla's opening try.

But the hero of the night was Trindall, who dislocated his shoulder against Canberra just four weeks ago.

The five-eighth spent most of the night awkwardly carrying his right arm, but was barely beaten in defence as the Cowboys failed to pick him out.

And while Trindall played with virtually one arm, he at least had his kicking boot.

Twice he forced an error out of Scott Drinkwater with his mid-field bombs, with one of those leading to a Katoa first-half try from the ensuing scrum.

With his arm looking slightly more comfortable in the second half, Trindall then put Will Kennedy over for the decisive try with a long ball for his fullback to make it 26-12.

That was Trindall's 31st assist of the year, with no player having laid on more tries in 2026.

Trindall delayed surgery to be fit to play the finals, and while the No. 6 didn't look comfortable the good news for Cronulla is he got through the game.

The Sharks will no doubt need him next week if they are to cause an upset against the winner of Penrith or Sydney Roosters.

For a side who had the worst defensive record of any finalist of the NRL-era, the Cowboys did well to hang on in Saturday night's game for as long as they did.

In the first 20 minutes alone Cronulla had 79 per cent of the ball and 22 tackles on the Cowboys' line.

But unlike when they let in 82 points against the Roosters in round 22 and conceded 50 against Canberra last week, North Queensland kept turning up.

Tom Dearden twice denied Jesse Colquhoun close to the line, while Drinkwater and Braidon Burns pulled off a tremendous try-saver on KL Iro.

North Queensland even got back to 12-6 down at halftime through Burns, and 16-12 with 22 minutes to go when Dearden put on a long cut-out ball for Zac Laybutt.

But ultimately the pressure told, and while a late Jaxon Purdue try offered a faint hope the Sharks were never really endangered.

The only down side for Cronulla will be the crowd of 17,429, which marked the lowest for a final at Allianz Stadium since 2012.

Officials will no doubt point out that only an extra few thousand fans turned up than would have fit in at Shark Park, had they been able to play there.
